facts.about: Interglobe Aviation Ltd (Indigo) is India’s largest passenger airline operating as a low-cost carrier. Serving 86 destinations including 24 international destinations, it provides passengers with a simple, unbundled product, fulfilling its singular brand promise of providing “low fares, on-time flights, and a courteous and hassle-free service” to its customers. IndiGo commenced operations in August 2006 with a single aircraft and has grown its fleet to 262 aircrafts.

flags.text: Cash-rich profits: 5-yr operating cash = 1274% of PAT

business.summary: InterGlobe Aviation Limited operates passenger airline services, primarily under the IndiGo brand, and generates revenue through passenger ticket sales, cancellation fees, and related aviation services.

narrative.scoreline: Management delivered on unit revenue expansion promises but profitability remains severely depressed by elevated operating and fuel costs.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Fuel cost environment and seasonal softness drove net loss of ₹1,900 crore in Q2 FY27.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Sep 2026 net loss was ₹1,879 crore with operating margin dropping to 8%.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Q1 FY27 total income grew ~19% YoY to ₹256 billion with net loss of ₹2.4 billion.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Jun 2026 revenue rose 19.9% YoY to ₹24,584 crore with net loss of ₹238 crore.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Dec 2025 operational disruptions led to over 2,500 cancellations.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Mar 2026 revenue growth slowed to 1.3% YoY and net loss fell to ₹2,537 crore.

bull: Sep 2026 top-line expansion of 25.9% YoY to ₹23,364 crore validates strong pricing power.
Robust operating cash flows of ₹23,470 crore in FY26 supported ₹21,767 crore free cash flow generation.
Fleet scale expanded with 57 aircraft deliveries in 2025, solidifying market leadership.
bear: Leverage remains extreme with debt at 17.5x equity on borrowings of ₹87,303 crore.
Net losses persisted across recent quarters, including ₹1,879 crore loss in Sep 2026.
Full-year FY26 swung to a net loss of ₹2,394 crore compared to ₹7,258 crore profit in FY25.
watch: Check Dec 2026 revenue growth against >25% PRASK guidance target.

claims.claim: Reported a net loss of 19 billion rupees due to exceptionally high fuel costs and a seasonally soft period.
claims.quote: However, due to the elevated cost environment, we reported a net loss of 19 billion rupees.

claims.claim: Concluded widebody damp-lease operations effectively from November 1st for economic prudence.
claims.quote: In this volatile environment, we considered it economically prudent to conclude our widebody damp-lease operations with effect from 1st November.

claims.claim: Reported total income of 256 billion rupees, up ~19% YoY, with yield growth of 21.3% and net loss of 2.4 billion rupees.
claims.quote: Moving to the financial performance for Q1 FY27, we reported a total income of 256 billion rupees, a growth of around 19% year over year, with a yield growth of 21.3% and a load factor reduction of 1.3%.

claims.claim: June quarter capacity growth came in at 3% YoY, broadly in line with guidance.
claims.quote: June quarter’s capacity growth came in at 3% on a year-over-year basis, broadly in line with our guidance.

claims.claim: Fuel CASK increased by around 80% year-on-year due to a 50% rise in Brent and 120% rise in Singapore jet fuel prices.
claims.quote: Despite this measure, our fuel CASK increased by around 80% year-on-year.

claims.claim: Inducted 13 aircraft, redelivered 9 original orderbook and 13 damp-leased aircraft, closing fleet at 432.
claims.quote: We inducted a total of 13 aircraft from our original orderbook... We redelivered 9 aircraft from our original orderbook and 13 damp-leased aircraft during the quarter resulting in a total closing fleet of 432 aircraft at the quarter end.

claims.claim: Middle East capacity is currently operating in the north of 90% levels.
claims.quote: Today, probably it's going to be in the north of 90% capacity that we are operating.

claims.claim: Early December operational disruptions led to cancellations of over 2,500 flights and delays of hundreds of flights.
claims.quote: Now, I want to address the operational disruptions that began in the first week of December and that led to cancellations of more than 2,500 flights and delays of hundreds of flights

claims.claim: In calendar year 2025, IndiGo received 57 aircraft and was the largest recipient of Airbus aircraft globally for the second consecutive year.
claims.quote: In terms of fleet addition, in the calendar year 2025 we received deliveries of 57 aircraft from our original orderbook... position as the largest recipient of Airbus aircraft globally for the second consecutive year
